questionText:
Changes to vegetation cover and other human activities influence carbon and nitrogen levels in soil, though how deep these effects extend is unclear. questionText:

questionText:
The north celestial pole (NCP)—the fixed point around which stars in the Northern Hemisphere (including the Sun) appear to rotate—is discernible only at night. Inspired by the navigational strategies of some insects and birds, researchers devised a method for locating the NCP in daytime using skylight polarization, which occurs as atmospheric particles scatter sunlight. A polarimetric camera captures images of polarization patterns, which rotate as the Sun’s position in the sky changes; temporal variances across images can then be used to determine an observer’s latitude and bearing relative to the NCP. Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text? 
A) It illustrates how most navigational tools utilize the NCP, recounts how researchers discovered that certain animals are able to navigate without using the NCP, and then proposes that this discovery could be used to avoid problems in navigation associated with reliance on the NCP. 
B) It presents a celestial-based method of navigation, enumerates the comparative benefits of an alternative method used by certain animals that is based on an unrelated natural occurrence, and then indicates how researchers assessed the relative accuracy of the two methods. 
C) It explains how the NCP is typically located, emphasizes a key difference between how humans and certain animals use the NCP for navigation, and then suggests an alternative way of using the NCP to improve existing navigational instruments. 
D) It notes an obstacle to observing an astronomical phenomenon, mentions a navigational ability of certain animals that inspired a solution to that obstacle, and then explains how researchers used an optical device to mimic that ability

questionText:

questionText:

questionText:

questionText:

For example, the symbol signifying the word huipil (blouse) in some contexts could signify the syllable "pil" in others, as in the place name "Chipiltepec." questionText:

questionText:

questionText:

questionText:

questionText:
The following text is adapted from Lewis Carroll’s 1889 satirical novel Sylvie and Bruno. A crowd has gathered outside a room belonging to the Warden, an official who reports to the Lord Chancellor. One man, who was more excited than the rest, flung his hat high into the air, and shouted (as well as I could make out) “Who roar for the Sub-Warden?” Everybody roared, but whether it was for the Sub-Warden, or not, did not clearly appear: some were shouting “Bread!” and some “Taxes!”, but no one seemed to know what it was they really wanted. All this I saw from the open window of the Warden’s breakfast-saloon, looking across the shoulder of the Lord Chancellor. “What can it all mean?” he kept repeating to himself. “I never heard such shouting before—and at this time of the morning, too! questionText:
In 2024, the city of Lenton planted shade trees along three blocks that had few mature trees. Summer pavement temperatures on those blocks fell by an average of 4°C, and pedestrians reported that the sidewalks felt more comfortable. The program requires regular watering during the trees' first two years, adding to maintenance costs. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) Pedestrians in Lenton prefer walking only on streets with mature trees.
B) Watering young trees is the largest expense in Lenton's annual budget.
C) Pavement temperature is determined entirely by the number of nearby trees.
D) Lenton's tree-planting program produced measurable benefits but also created maintenance needs.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: D is correct because it captures both the program's benefits and its maintenance requirement. The other choices elevate a detail or make a claim the text does not support.

questionText:
Marine biologists attached fragments of the same coral species to restoration frames at four reef sites. Survival rates differed sharply among the sites. When the researchers later matched coral strains to the temperature and water-flow conditions at each site, survival improved. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) Matching coral strains to local conditions can improve restoration outcomes.
B) All coral strains survive equally well when attached to metal frames.
C) Water flow is the only factor that affects restored coral.
D) Coral restoration is possible only at four reef sites.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: A is correct. It expresses the passage's central finding, while the other choices misstate or overgeneralize individual details.

questionText:
A public library extended its weekday hours from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. During the next three months, evening visits increased substantially, especially among adults who reported working during the day. The library board is now considering whether to make the schedule permanent. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) The library board has already made the new schedule permanent.
B) Most daytime library visitors are adults who do not work.
C) Later hours appear to have expanded library access, particularly for working adults.
D) The library receives no visitors before 6 p.m.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: C is correct because it synthesizes the schedule change and the most important attendance result. The other options contradict or exaggerate secondary information.

questionText:
Some bees release pollen by vibrating their flight muscles while gripping a flower. In an experiment, two bee species produced vibrations at different average frequencies, but both released similar amounts of pollen from the same plant species. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) Only one bee species can release pollen by vibrating flowers.
B) Different vibration patterns can be similarly effective at releasing pollen.
C) The plant species in the experiment produces no pollen without bees.
D) Vibration frequency always determines how much pollen a bee releases.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: B is correct. The key result is that different average frequencies produced similar pollen release; the species and plant are supporting details.

questionText:
Chemical analysis of pottery from an ancient coastal settlement showed that most vessels were made with local clay. Several vessels, however, contained decorative minerals found only in a region hundreds of kilometers inland. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) All pottery at the settlement was imported from inland communities.
B) Coastal potters avoided decorating vessels made from local clay.
C) The settlement had no access to materials from distant regions.
D) Local pottery production likely incorporated some materials obtained through long-distance exchange.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: D is correct because it combines the local-clay evidence with the presence of distant minerals. The other choices conflict with one or both findings.

questionText:
After a former parking area was restored as a wetland, the site held more stormwater during heavy rain and supported more bird species than it had previously. Managers must still remove invasive plants each spring to maintain those gains. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) The restored wetland provides ecological and flood-control benefits that require continued management.
B) Removing invasive plants prevents all flooding near the former parking area.
C) Bird species avoid wetlands that are managed in the spring.
D) The parking area stored more stormwater than the restored wetland.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: A is correct because it captures the overall benefits and the need for upkeep. The other choices distort particular details.

questionText:
In one introductory programming course, students alternated between writing code and reviewing a partner's code. On later assignments, these students identified errors more accurately and explained their solutions more clearly than students who had practiced only writing code. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) Reviewing code is useful only after students have mastered programming.
B) Students who write code should never work with a partner.
C) Alternating between producing and reviewing code may strengthen debugging and explanation skills.
D) The students who reviewed code completed fewer assignments.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: C is correct because it states the broad instructional implication supported by both reported outcomes. The remaining choices are unsupported or contradictory.

questionText:
Sensors placed on a glacier initially reported rapid afternoon melting. Engineers discovered that direct sunlight was heating the sensors themselves. After the sensors were fitted with reflective shields, the afternoon readings aligned with measurements from nearby instruments. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) Reflective shields cause glaciers to melt more slowly.

C) Nearby instruments cannot measure afternoon glacier conditions.
D) Glacier sensors produce reliable data only before noon.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: B is correct. The central point is that sunlight distorted the original measurements and that shielding corrected the problem.

questionText:
A housing cooperative installed gardens on three flat roofs. The gardens reduced summer roof temperatures and absorbed some rainfall, but the cooperative had to reinforce one older roof before planting. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: C is correct. The choice captures both the reported benefits and the limited structural challenge instead of isolating one detail.

questionText:
Speakers of the Nami language created weekly conversation groups and recorded elders telling traditional stories. After two years, more teenagers could hold basic conversations, though few had yet reached advanced fluency. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

D) Community programs increased basic Nami use among teenagers, while advanced fluency remained uncommon.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: D is correct. The choice includes the program's progress and its remaining limitation.

questionText:
Researchers placed coconut shells and plain stones in an aquarium with octopuses. Several octopuses carried the shells and later assembled them as shelters, whereas they rarely moved the stones. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: A is correct. The choice summarizes the meaningful contrast between carrying useful shells and rarely moving stones.

questionText:
A neighborhood installed low sound barriers beside a busy road. Measurements showed that the barriers reduced noise on ground-floor patios but had little effect on upper-floor balconies. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

explanation: B is correct. The choice states the overall finding and the important difference by elevation.

questionText:
Excavations revealed that an ancient road was repaired repeatedly with local stone. Pottery from distant regions was found beside several repair layers, suggesting that travelers continued using the route over many generations. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

D) Only local goods moved along the road.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: C is correct. The choice integrates the repair and pottery evidence into the passage's central historical conclusion.

questionText:
A university café introduced reusable cups with a refundable deposit. Disposable-cup use fell sharply, but many reusable cups were not returned until the café added collection bins in residence halls. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: D is correct. The choice captures both the initial success and the operational improvement.

questionText:
A regional seed bank stores duplicate seed samples in two buildings with separate power systems. The arrangement costs more than using one facility, but it reduces the chance that a single equipment failure will destroy an entire collection. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: A is correct. The choice identifies the main tradeoff rather than focusing only on cost or location.

questionText:
A warehouse tested robots that choose routes independently rather than following fixed floor markings. The new robots adjusted more quickly when aisles were blocked, although they required more computing power. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

explanation: B is correct. The choice summarizes the benefit and cost of the new routing approach.

questionText:
A museum lowered light levels around delicate textiles and added focused lamps that activate when visitors approach. The textiles now receive less total light, while visitors report that labels remain easy to read. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

D) Focused lamps increased the textiles' total light exposure.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: C is correct. The choice captures the conservation goal and the maintained visitor experience.

questionText:
Trees in one forest exchanged carbon with nearby seedlings through fungal networks. The transfers were small compared with the carbon seedlings produced themselves, but they increased when seedlings were heavily shaded. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) Seedlings obtained all their carbon from fungal networks.
B) Carbon transfer stopped when seedlings were shaded.
C) Trees transferred equal amounts under every condition.
D) Fungal networks supplied limited carbon to seedlings, with larger transfers under deep shade.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: D is correct. The choice preserves both the small scale of the transfers and the shade-related increase.

questionText:
After a city reduced bus fares on weekends, ridership increased most on routes serving parks and shopping districts. Weekday ridership changed little because weekday fares remained the same. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) Lower weekend fares increased weekend travel, especially to recreational and shopping destinations.

C) Ridership fell on every route serving a park.
D) The fare change affected weekday and weekend travel equally.

explanation: A is correct. The choice states the main effect and where it was strongest.

questionText:
A translator preserved the short lines of a poem but changed several images that would have been obscure to readers in the target language. The translation therefore resembles the original rhythm more closely than its imagery. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) The translator reproduced every image word for word.
B) The translator prioritized the poem's rhythmic form while adapting some of its imagery.
C) The translation abandoned the poem's short lines.
D) Readers in the target language rejected all poetic imagery.
teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: B is correct. The choice describes the translator's central tradeoff between form and imagery.

questionText:
Farmers near a dormant volcano noticed that fields containing thin layers of old volcanic ash retained water longer than nearby sandy fields. Very thick ash layers, however, restricted root growth. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

questionText:
On reefs where large predatory fish returned after fishing limits were introduced, some smaller fish spent more time close to coral shelter. Their overall population still increased because the reefs also contained more food and healthier coral. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

questionText:
A mill began recycling paper fibers more times before discarding them. This reduced demand for new pulp, but fibers became shorter with each cycle and eventually had to be mixed with fresh material. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

questionText:
A high school shifted its start time forty minutes later. Students reported sleeping longer on school nights, while participation in early-morning clubs declined until the clubs were rescheduled. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

questionText:
Biologists compared satellite images with field surveys to count seals on remote beaches. Images allowed more beaches to be checked, but field surveys were still needed where rocks and shadows resembled animals. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

questionText:
Urban bats used newly installed roost boxes most often when the boxes faced morning sun but were shaded in the afternoon. Boxes exposed to sun all day became too warm during summer. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

explanation: D is correct. The choice synthesizes the use pattern and the temperature evidence.

questionText:
An open-source microscope can be assembled from widely available parts, allowing schools to repair it locally. Its images are less detailed than those from advanced laboratory microscopes but sufficient for many introductory lessons. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

teachingTopic: 区分主要信息与次要信息
explanation: A is correct. The choice captures the device's practical advantage and technical limitation.

questionText:
A town sends household food scraps to a composting facility instead of a landfill. The program reduces landfill waste, but contamination from plastic bags slows processing and requires additional sorting. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

explanation: B is correct. The choice summarizes both the program's benefit and its operational challenge.

questionText:
Historians compared several maps of the same nineteenth-century harbor. Later maps show new warehouses but omit small fishing docks still mentioned in tax records, indicating that mapmakers emphasized different features for different users. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

explanation: C is correct. The choice accounts for both newly mapped warehouses and deliberately omitted docks.

questionText:
A lecture hall installed wall panels that absorb echoes. Students seated at the back reported clearer speech, while students near the front noticed little change because speech had already been clear there. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

questionText:
American fashion designer Patrick Kelly was known for his love of colorful buttons. Many of his signature dresses feature bold assortments of buttons throughout the garment. questionText:
A museum curator is writing a biographical statement about Trinidadian-born Chinese dancer, choreographer, and teacher Dai Ailian for a new exhibit on Chinese dance. The curator claims that some of the pieces Dai created shortly after arriving in mainland China in 1941, such as the solo dance Yao Drum, reflect a desire to represent the dances of local communities Dai visited during her travels through China. Which quotation from a work by a dance historian would be the most effective evidence for the curator to include in support of this claim?

questionText:
Many mosquito repellents contain natural components that work by activating multiple odor receptors on mosquitoes’ antennae. As the insects develop resistance, new repellents are needed. questionText:
Birds of many species ingest foods containing carotenoids, pigmented molecules that are converted into feather coloration. Coloration tends to be especially saturated in male birds’ feathers, and because carotenoids also confer health benefits, the deeply saturated colors generally serve to communicate what is known as an honest signal of a bird’s overall fitness to potential mates. However, ornithologist Allison J. Shultz and others have found that males in several species of the tanager genus Ramphocelus use microstructures in their feathers to manipulate light, creating the appearance of deeper saturation without the birds necessarily having to maintain a carotenoid-rich diet. These findings suggest that _______ Which choice most logically completes the text?

B) feather microstructures may be less effective than deeply saturated feathers for signaling overall fitness.

questionText:
The domestic sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) descends from a wild plant native to South America. It also populates the Polynesian Islands, where evidence confirms that Native Hawaiians and other Indigenous peoples were cultivating the plant centuries before seafaring first occurred over the thousands of miles of ocean separating them from South America. To explain how the sweet potato was first introduced in Polynesia, botanist Pablo Muñoz-Rodríguez and colleagues analyzed the DNA of numerous varieties of the plant, concluding that Polynesian varieties diverged from South American ones over 100,000 years ago. Given that Polynesia was peopled only in the last three thousand years, the team concluded that ______ Which choice most logically completes the text? 
A) the cultivation of the sweet potato in Polynesia likely predates its cultivation in South America. 
B) Polynesian peoples likely acquired the sweet potato from South American peoples only within the last three thousand years. 
C) human activity likely played no role in the introduction of the sweet potato in Polynesia.

questionText:
The morphological novelty of echinoderms—marine invertebrates with radial symmetry, usually starlike, around a central point—impedes comparisons with most other animals, in which bilateral symmetry on an anterior-posterior (head to tail) axis through a trunk is typical. Particularly puzzling are sea stars, thought to have evolved a headless layout from a known bilateral origin. Applying genomic knowledge of Saccoglossus kowalevskii acorn worms (close relatives of sea stars, and thus expected to have similar markers for corresponding anatomical regions) to the body patterning genes of Patiria miniata sea stars, Laurent Formery et al. observed activity only in anterior genes across P. miniata’s entire body and some posterior genes limited to the edges, suggesting that _______ Which choice most logically completes the text? 
A) despite the greater prevalence of anterior genes in sea stars’ genetic makeup, posterior genes active at the body’s perimeter are primarily responsible for the starlike layout that distinguishes sea stars’ radial symmetry from that of other echinoderms. 
B) contrary to the belief that they evolved from early ancestors with the bilateral form typical of many other animals, sea stars instead originated with an atypical body layout that was neither bilaterally nor radially symmetrical.

questionText:
In documents called judicial opinions, judges explain the reasoning behind their legal rulings, and in those explanations they sometimes cite and discuss historical and contemporary philosophers. Legal scholar and philosopher Anita L. Allen argues that while judges are naturally inclined to mention philosophers whose views align with their own positions, the strongest judicial opinions consider and rebut potential objections; discussing philosophers whose views conflict with judges’ views could therefore _______ Which choice most logically completes the text? 
A) allow judges to craft judicial opinions without needing to consult philosophical works.

questionText:
Although military veterans make up a small proportion of the total population of the United States, they occupy a significantly higher proportion of the jobs in the civilian government. questionText:
Among social animals that care for their young, such as chickens, macaque monkeys, and humans, newborns appear to show an innate attraction to faces and face-like stimuli. Elisabetta Versace and her colleagues used an image of three black dots arranged in the shape of eyes and a nose or mouth to test whether this trait also occurs in Testudo tortoises, which live alone and do not engage in parental care. They found that tortoise hatchlings showed a significant preference for the image, suggesting that ______ Which choice most logically completes the text? 
A) face-like stimuli are likely perceived as harmless by newborns of social species that practice parental care but as threatening by newborns of solitary species without parental care. 
B) researchers should not assume that an innate attraction to face-like stimuli is necessarily an adaptation related to social interaction or parental care.

questionText:
Aptamers—synthetic DNA or RNA molecules that bind to target molecules—can be used to test for foodborne bacterial pathogens, though their specificity (the probability of returning a negative result in the absence of the focal pathogen) in real-world foods has been unclear. Sandeep Somvanshi et al. fabricated test paper incorporating aptamers targeting strain O157:H7 of the bacteria Escherichia coli; the paper shifts from pink to purple as the aptamers bind to target molecules. Somvanshi et al. tested the paper in store-bought pear juice they treated with E. coli O157:H7, other strains of E. coli, or other bacteria species. Following exposure, the paper from the O157:H7 test was purple while papers from the other tests were pink, suggesting that _______ Which choice most logically completes the text? 
A) aptamer-based tests in real-world foods are more likely to show a high degree of specificity if the focal pathogen is E. coli O157:H7 than if the focal pathogen is another strain of E. coli or another species. 
B) uncertainty about the specificity of aptamer-based tests for pathogens in real-world foods may be due to the similarity between E. coli O157:H7 and other E. coli strains. 
C) the specificity of the tests in a real-world food was unaffected by the aptamers’ tendency to bind to different strains of E. coli. 
D) the aptamers successfully bound to E. coli O157:H7 and the tests displayed a high degree of specificity in a real-world food

questionText:
Euphorbia esula (leafy spurge) is a Eurasian plant that has become invasive in North America, where it displaces native vegetation and sickens cattle. Recent research on introducing engineered DNA into plant species to inhibit their reproduction may offer a path toward exclusively targeting E. esula, consequently _______ Which choice most logically completes the text?

questionText:
A team of biologists led by Jae-Hoon Jung, Antonio D. Barbosa, and Stephanie Hutin investigated the mechanism that allows Arabidopsis thaliana (thale cress) plants to accelerate flowering at high temperatures. They replaced the protein ELF3 in the plants with a similar protein found in another species (stiff brome) that, unlike A. thaliana, displays no acceleration in flowering with increased temperature. A comparison of unmodified A. thaliana plants with the altered plants showed no difference in flowering at 22° Celsius, but at 27° Celsius, the unmodified plants exhibited accelerated flowering while the altered ones did not, which suggests that _______ Which choice most logically completes the text?

questionText:

The team found a tablet in Merneith’s tomb with writing suggesting that she was in charge of the country’s treasury and other central offices. Whether Merneith was a pharaoh or not, this discovery supports the idea that Merneith likely _______ Which choice most logically completes the text?

questionText:
In a study of the cognitive abilities of white-faced capuchin monkeys (Cebus imitator), researchers neglected to control for the physical difficulty of the tasks they used to evaluate the monkeys. The cognitive abilities of monkeys given problems requiring little dexterity, such as sliding a panel to retrieve food, were judged by the same criteria as were those of monkeys given physically demanding problems, such as unscrewing a bottle and inserting a straw. questionText:
Researchers Eugeni Vidal-Tortosa and Robin Lovelace looked at the relationship between street lighting in a city and people’s willingness to ride a bicycle. Their results suggest that poor street lighting can deter new or inexperienced cyclists from riding in a city but has little effect on experienced cyclists. Therefore, increasing the number of streetlights in a city could potentially _______ Which choice most logically completes the text?

questionText:
Like many other genera of wild bees, bumblebees have in recent decades experienced population collapse caused by, among other factors, habitat destruction and climate variation. Bumblebees are also one of the most researched bee genera, second only to honeybees. As a result, ecologists have gained much of their insight about wild-bee declines from bumblebees. In a 2021 paper, zoologist Guillaume Ghisbain notes that bumblebees are among the relatively few wild-bee genera that display social behaviors and dietary generalism (ability to obtain nectar and pollen from a diversity of plant species), two traits that are associated with increased resilience to some specific environmental changes. Ghisbain therefore contends that _______ Which choice most logically completes the text? 
A) although bumblebees and many other wild bees have experienced similar population declines in the past, compared with other wild bees, bumblebees are likely at greater risk of being harmed by climate variation than by habitat destruction. 
B) although bumblebees have been more extensively studied than most wild bees, researchers should not use bumblebees to draw conclusions about the decline of other wild bees, even ones with feeding patterns and levels of sociability that are similar to those of bumblebees. 
C) because bumblebees and other bees with generalist diets are less negatively affected by environmental stress than bees with specialized diets are, they are less likely to experience major population changes in the future than bees with specialized diets are. 
D) because the responses of bumblebees and other wild bees to environmental threats are not always comparable, researchers need to exercise caution when extrapolating information about wild-bee population declines from bumblebees
teachingTopic: 完成逻辑上最合理的句子或结论

questionText:
In Switzerland, the white fuzzy mountain flowers known as edelweiss are widely treated as a symbol of strength and courage. Historian Tobias Scheidegger has shown that the popular view of the flowers originated in the mid-1800s when mountain climbing became popular in Switzerland. Mountain climbers spread the idea that the flowers grew only in steep, icy terrains that were dangerous to climb to. Scheidegger says that these claims were self- interested. He suggests that mountain climbers presented edelweiss in this way in order to _______ Which choice most logically completes the text?

questionText:
The ratio of methane to other atmospheric constituents—represented by a measure called the methane mole fraction—influences a variety of meteorological phenomena, notably precipitation and humidity. Juan Lora and colleagues point out that outputs of the IPSL atmospheric model of Titan, which track closely to observations in some respects, reflect how the model’s developers responded to this challenge: by prescribing a uniform methane mole fraction for the lowest level of the atmosphere. questionText:
To understand how temperature change affects microorganism-mediated cycling of soil nutrients in alpine ecosystems, Eva Kaštovská et al. collected plant-soil cores in the Tatra Mountains at elevations around 2,100 meters and transplanted them to elevations of 1,700–1,800 meters, where the mean air temperature was warmer by 2°C. questionText:

questionText:

questionText:

questionText:

explanation: A is correct. The shrub's variable flowering date tracks variable rainy-season timing better than a fixed date, implying the value of biological cues.

questionText:
Analysis of paintings from a seventeenth-century workshop found that an expensive blue pigment appeared mainly in thin final layers. Less costly pigments were used in the thicker layers underneath, even where the finished surface appeared blue. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:
A transit agency tested two station maps: one labeled exits with text only, and one used both text and widely recognized icons. explanation: B is correct. The icon-enhanced map specifically improved navigation for visitors who spoke other languages, implying greater cross-language accessibility.

questionText:
A café moved its unsweetened drinks to the first page of the menu while leaving prices and recipes unchanged. Orders of those drinks increased during the next month. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:

questionText:
A park replaced text-heavy trail signs with signs that combined brief text and pictograms. International visitors asked rangers for directions less often, while local visitors' behavior changed little. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:
Pottery fragments from several workshops carry distinctive maker's marks. At a distant trading center, archaeologists found vessels bearing marks from all those workshops. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:
An online course added captions to all lectures. Completion rates rose most among students studying in noisy shared spaces, even though the lecture audio did not change. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:

questionText:
A city added flexible posts between a bicycle lane and parked cars. Reports of cars entering the lane fell, although the width and route of the lane stayed the same. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:

questionText:
A grocery store introduced smaller carts beside its standard carts. Shoppers buying only a few items selected the smaller carts most often and spent less time waiting to return carts after checkout. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:
An astronomy club covered flashlights with red filters during observing sessions. Members needed less time to readjust to the dark after checking star charts. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:
After a local archive digitized its most fragile newspapers, researchers consulted the digital copies frequently while requests to handle the originals declined. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:
A plaza fountain was programmed to operate during the hottest afternoon hours rather than early morning. More visitors gathered near it in the afternoon, but morning use of the plaza remained similar. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:
In a row of otherwise similar buildings, roofs coated with a pale material were cooler at midday than dark roofs. Indoor temperatures differed most on the top floors. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

questionText:
Seed packets were redesigned to show both planting depth and a simple depth diagram. Novice gardeners made fewer planting-depth errors, while experienced gardeners' results were unchanged. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

A) Tree canopy definitely causes all changes in summer surface temperature.
B) Summer surface temperature cannot be related to tree canopy.
C) The variables are associated in the observed data, but the study alone does not establish that tree canopy causes changes in summer surface temperature.
D) The association proves that no third variable is involved.
teachingTopic: 相关关系与因果关系
explanation: C is correct. An observational association does not by itself establish causation.
